diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: The appellate court confirmed the prison sentence and permanent removal of clerical attire for Ahmad Heydari. He had previously been sentenced to three years, three months, and one day in prison, permanent removal of clerical attire, two years of prohibition from promotional activities, and permanent blocking of his personal channel. The appellate court suspended two-thirds of the prison sentence for five years.
Hassan Faraji, a citizen from Ilam, has been detained by security forces in this city for eight days, and there is still no information about his place of detention or his condition.

Marzieh Jafari, head coach of Khatoun Bam football team, won the Best Female Football Coach in Asia award for the second consecutive year. She won this award at the 2026 Asian Football Awards, surpassing Park Yoon Jung and Ma Xiaozhu. Jafari had also won this title last year.

A citizen accused Masoud Pezeshkian in a video sent to Iran International of deceiving people with electoral promises and said that the country's resources were spent on Lebanon, Palestine, Gaza, and proxy forces instead of Iran's infrastructure. He added that these problems were not created by the enemy but by Pezeshkian, calling him the enemy of the people.

Reports indicate the possibility of a large-scale renewed attack by the US against Iran. Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's Prime Minister, has pressured Washington to participate in a four to seven-day airstrike campaign against the Islamic Republic. The Pentagon has deployed extensive military equipment in the region, with bombers on 96-hour alert.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said in a trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, that the three leaders are "making history." The Ukraine war and major global issues were discussed, but the joint statement emphasized general principles of cooperation and did not directly mention the wars in Iran and Ukraine. Trump stressed the need to prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons, but there was no specific agreement on Iran in the statement.

Alireza Beiranvand, goalkeeper of Iran's national football team and Tractor, ended Iran's 22-year wait for the title by winning the 2026 Asian Player of the Year award. He won the award at the Asian Football Awards ceremony in Bangkok, ahead of Saudi nominees Salem Al-Dawsari and Firas Al-Buraikan. Beiranvand is the fifth Iranian player to receive this award.

A reception hall in Boukan was sealed. It was reported that a reception hall in Boukan was sealed for reasons including what was called "failure to observe social norms and customs," and the manager of this business unit was referred to the judicial authority.

Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and Xi Jinping held a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, discussing major international issues including the Ukraine war, Iran's nuclear program, and nuclear disarmament. The leaders emphasized the necessity of cooperation, mutual respect, and maintaining global peace and security.

Theo Francken, Belgium's defense minister, announced that his government will try to include Yemen's Houthis in the European Union's list of terrorist organizations. This stance comes while only a limited number of EU member states support this action.

Mostafa Tajzadeh, a political prisoner held in Evin Prison, was returned to Evin Prison after three nights of hospitalization. His wife stated that Tajzadeh was hospitalized for medical tests and examinations but was returned to prison before the tests were completed. It was also reported that some officers treated them inappropriately.

The International Court of Justice in The Hague ruled on Thursday, 28 Aban, with 9 judges in favor and 6 against, that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority during the 2017 military operations. The court also ordered Myanmar to ensure the safe return of Rohingya refugees and to prosecute those responsible for the genocide. This ruling was issued following a complaint by Gambia in 2019 and based on the 1948 Genocide Convention.

Tina (Tooba) Moradi Moghui, a detainee related to the nationwide protests of Dey 1404, was released from Varamin Qarchak Prison on Tuesday, 26 Aban 1405 under electronic monitoring. Her release was made with a bail of two billion tomans. She will serve the remainder of her sentence outside prison with travel restrictions.

Mehdi Tartaar, Persepolis coach, denied rumors of discord in his team's locker room in a press conference before the match against Paykan and reported the readiness of national players after international matches. He emphasized that Persepolis must win this match and also commented on the injured players and the possibility of hiring a foreign assistant.

The second branch of the Yazd Revolutionary Court issued sentences for four detainees of the January 1404 protests and defendants in the Yazd Telecommunications case. Pouya Fakhrabadi was sentenced to death, and Mehdi Rajabi, Mohammad Kargar, and Mohini Maki each received 20 years of exile imprisonment. These individuals are currently held in Yazd prison.
A video shows that on 27 Aban students at a girls' high school in Mashhad sang the anthem "Nam-e Javid Vatan" together.

Hossein Mohseni, spokesperson for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, said in a speech at the University of Tehran that the senior spokesperson of the Armed Forces General Staff had previously announced that media such as Iran International are targets of the Islamic Republic's armed forces. Abolfazl Shekarchi, the senior spokesperson of the armed forces, had earlier threatened Iran International, BBC Persian, Radio Farda, and their staff with being placed on the list of military targets.

Vladimir Putin, President of Russia, said after a trilateral meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping that he has no doubt Trump is "sincerely" trying to resolve disputes, including the war in Ukraine, and improve US-Russia relations. Putin added that Moscow wants this process to move faster and more effectively but acts based on "existing realities" and hopes Trump's approach continues.

Scott Busent, the US Treasury Secretary, predicted that Iran's economy will shrink by more than 25 percent within one year. These remarks come nearly three months after the start of the Trump administration's economic expulsion operation against the Islamic Republic. Mehdi Beigi reviewed the dimensions and achievements of this operation over the past three months in "Peyvast".

Amirhossein Bankipour, a member of the Cultural Commission of the Parliament, said that the implementation of the Youth Population Law has reduced the rate of voluntary pregnancy termination by 50 percent and has somewhat controlled the population decline trend in Iran.

Bloomberg reported, citing Western officials, that the likelihood of a new round of extensive US attacks against Iran has increased. Donald Trump has not made a final decision but is considering another attack. Benjamin Netanyahu has requested a joint air operation against Iran, while European governments and Gulf Arab states urge restraint from extensive attacks.

France, Germany, Britain, and the United States expressed concern about ambiguities in the nuclear activities of the Islamic Republic and demanded immediate access for the International Atomic Energy Agency to the Isfahan facilities. These four countries also stated that the agency's information on Iran's enriched uranium stockpiles has not been updated since Esfand 1404.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, made recommendations to the public to reduce energy consumption and made remarks about sleeping with a jacket, which sparked reactions from citizens. Several viewers sent messages to Iran International's media platform criticizing him. One citizen said Pezeshkian sleeps with a jacket and clothes on so that if necessary, he can take shelter in a tunnel or bunker.

Hassan Roshan, an Iranian football veteran, said in an interview with Haft Varzeshi about Alireza Beiranvand being chosen as Asia's best player of the year: "We were always happy when an Iranian won the Asian Man of the Year award, but this time I am upset because Beiranvand showed his low side."

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing smoke rising from the Behbahan refinery and spreading in the city's sky. He said this pollution is really carcinogenic for the people of Behbahan. The situation of this refinery has made the city's air very polluted and dangerous.
The commander of the police in Somesara reported the arrest of a citizen in this county due to what was described as "spreading false information and disturbing public opinion in cyberspace."

The United States, Russia, and China signed a joint statement titled "Peace Declaration" at the end of a trilateral meeting. The statement emphasizes reducing nuclear risks, reforming the United Nations structure, stabilizing energy markets, and respecting the immunity of official country representatives.

The family of Robert Levinson, a former FBI agent who disappeared in Iran, wants to seize nearly one and a half billion dollars from a Malaysian bank. The US Court of Appeals is addressing this request today. Levinson's family considers Kuwait Finance House linked to the Iranian government and has previously obtained a default judgment against the Islamic Republic.

The Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the Houthi attacks on civilian and economic facilities in Riyadh on Thursday, 28 Aban, stating that these attacks damaged the King Abdullah Financial Center. The ministry called the attacks "terrorist" and said Saudi Arabia will not yield to attacks on its land and facilities. Additionally, the official Saudi news agency, SPA, reported that the Houthi attack on a tower in Riyadh's financial district caused damage to several floors and surrounding buildings, but no one was injured.

The Saudi Civil Defense Organization announced on Thursday, 28 Aban, that a tower in Riyadh's financial center was damaged during a Houthi attack from Yemen. The attack caused material damage to several floors of the tower and adjacent buildings, but no casualties or injuries have been reported. Rescue teams and relevant authorities have immediately arrived at the scene and started necessary measures to secure the area and assess the damage.
A video sent to Iran International shows that the slogan "Long live the Shah" was written overnight on a wall in Urmia.

Vladimir Putin said that until the political leaders of some European countries change, Russia-Europe relations will not be fully restored. Mark Carney said Canada wants a trade agreement with the US, but if Washington is unwilling, Canada will expand trade with other countries.

The number of detainees related to the protest gathering in Abdanan county has reached eight. Another citizen named Shahram Javidaneh has been added to this group. So far, there is no information about the location or condition of the detainees.

"GTA 6", the latest game by Rockstar, will be released on Thursday, 28 Aban. However, Iranian gamers face sanctions, slow and limited internet, and a 40% increase in internet tariffs. Iranian users have expressed regret about experiencing this game on social media.

Donald Trump said in an interview with NBC News about his trip to China and meetings with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin that everything went great and excellent relations were formed. He added that he and Xi Jinping believe that setting at least minimum regulatory frameworks for artificial intelligence is a positive step. When asked about the meaning of "minimum level," Trump said they did not enter into discussions about definitions.

The death of oil industry workers in a bus rollover accident sparked new protests in Abdanan. Despite memories of the killing of protesters in Dey 1404 and the risks of death, arrest, and torture, the people of Abdanan took to the streets again. Reports indicate security forces clashed with protesters, fired tear gas, shot in the air, and arrested several citizens, including a 15-year-old teenager.
On the evening of Thursday, 28 Aban, following security forces shooting at two citizens riding a motorcycle in Sarbaz County, one person was killed and another injured.

Shervin Savadkoohi said the Neka intelligence office repeatedly summoned and threatened Farzad Khosh-Bersh's father and sister in the week leading up to his memorial ceremony. Agents told Khosh-Bersh's father he might die in a car accident on his way back to work in Asaluyeh. The intelligence office also asked the family for a list of guests and speech texts and told some of Khosh-Bersh's friends they were not allowed to attend the ceremony, but the family held the event despite the threats.

Satellite images show the spread of oil slicks near the United Arab Emirates waters reaching the country's shores. Wim Zwijnenburg, an environmental expert at Pax, told Reuters that satellite images from November 18 show oil slicks from a ship fire have reached the UAE shores. Sarbananda Sonowal, India's shipping minister, had earlier stated that the ship was attacked on November 11 while near Mina Saqr port in the UAE.

Three months of overdue payments to retired armed forces personnel have not been paid. According to an activist from the armed forces fund, out of the four months of overdue payments, only one month will be paid along with the November salary.

Reza Najafi, Iran's representative to the International Atomic Energy Agency, warned that information collected from Iran's nuclear facilities by the agency "will certainly be used for further attacks." He supported the joint statement by China, Iran, and Russia and opposed removing Rafael Grossi's report from the list of confidential documents. Najafi described Grossi's remarks about the interruption of the agency's continuous awareness of Iran's nuclear activities as incomplete and uncertain, stating that Iran has cooperated extensively with the agency.

A death row prisoner in Ramian County, Golestan Province, was released from execution due to the victim's family's pardon. Also, the judicial deputy and dispute resolution official of Kerman Province reported the release of 15 death row prisoners in this province during the first seven months of the current year.
Due to lack of workplace safety and unsuitable conditions, an electrician worker in Tehran had an accident while working and died.

Donald Trump said in an interview with Barak Ravid that he has not yet decided on the next actions of the US in the war with Iran. Trump said he is not in a hurry to decide about Iran and they must see what happens after January 1. Ravid reported that Trump is under pressure from Netanyahu for a quick return to war and is still considering another attack on Iran.

Saberin news agency, affiliated with the IRGC, reported that the Islamic Republic is considering resuming oil exports despite the US naval blockade. The agency wrote that dozens of Iranian tankers are preparing to head towards China. It also announced that Tehran has warned regional countries that it will enter a war if the US attacks tankers bound for China.
Today, Thursday 28 Aban, a group of unemployed youth in Gachsaran held a protest for the second consecutive day by blocking the route to the county's petro-refinery.
The Domino audio version reports that the people of Abdanan have returned to the streets.

At least 3 protest gatherings were held today, Thursday 28 Aban, including workers of Kaveh Sodium Carbonate Company in Firouzabad protesting living conditions. Bakers in Ahvaz gathered in front of Khuzestan Governor's Office. Also, unemployed youth in Gachsaran blocked the road to the petro-refinery for the second consecutive day.

According to Samira Qaraei, Vladimir Putin's presence at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit after nine years has attracted much attention on social media. Users are analyzing his body language and behavior alongside Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. Many believe these images indicate that Putin was not the distinguished guest at the summit as the Kremlin tries to portray.
Abdelhay Dashti, a resident of Chabahar, was summoned and interrogated by the Intelligence of the Revolutionary Guards in this city on Tuesday, 26 Aban.
It was reported in the audio version 24 with Fardad Farahzad that Trump is seeking a widespread attack on the Islamic Republic.

Sanaz Yekta, a resident of Tehran, was summoned by the Tehran Security Prosecutor's Office and appeared there on Tuesday, 25 Aban. The charges against her include "propaganda against the regime" and interviews with foreign media. She was summoned by the Ministry of Intelligence's follow-up office in early Mehr, detained, and later released on bail.

FIFA announced the names of three candidates for the presidency election of the organization in 2027. Gianni Infantino, Philippe Diallo, and Kozo Tashima are the candidates. The election will be held on March 18 in Rabat, Morocco.

The International Football Federation released the latest national team rankings for 2026 after the November FIFA dates, with Spain maintaining first place despite a 3-2 loss to England. Morocco rose two places to fifth, their best ranking ever. Iran remained 23rd in the world and second in Asia, while Japan leads Asian football.

Reports from various cities in Iran have presented reactions to Masoud Pezeshkian's statements about people's problems. From Miandoab to Tehran, people have criticized the difficult living conditions and the government's inability to provide basic needs such as electricity and gas. Some have said Pezeshkian is unaware of the real situation of the people and that his salary is not equal to workers'.

Reuters reported that the US Senate rejected a resolution to limit Donald Trump's war powers against Iran by 51 votes against 48. The resolution, previously passed by the House of Representatives, would have required Trump to end the war with Iran or get congressional approval to continue it. The Senate vote was largely along party lines, with Republicans supporting Trump.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, referred to Hossein Mohabi, spokesperson for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, saying that Iran International is among the military targets of the Islamic Republic. He said that in today's world, one cannot speak to the media with the language of terror. He added that people choose which media to follow themselves, and Iran International journalists continue their work despite threats.

Farzin Nadimi said the US, by strengthening its military presence in the region, has the capability to conduct operations on the scale of past wars or even larger. He added that the Israeli army is also operationally ready and may join the US if it initiates operations. Nadimi also said increased IRGC attacks and US economic pressures have destabilized the situation, and both sides are ready for war but do not want to start it.

Gideon Sa'ar, Israel's Foreign Minister, said on Thursday, 28 Aban, that the Islamic Republic is trying to revive its nuclear program and is active in unconventional weapons. He described the threats against Israel as serious and real and said this issue should be considered in discussions about forming Israel's future government.

Sardar Mohibi, spokesperson for the IRGC, said the senior spokesperson of the Armed Forces General Staff announced that some media outlets, including Iran International, are "targets." He accused these media of "hostility" and "lack of neutrality." Mohibi also spoke about media competition to publish the "first narrative," saying this narrative is good if "accurate," but sometimes accuracy and correctness are sacrificed for speed.

Nahid Shashani, dubbing director and voice actress, passed away on Thursday night at the age of 77 after months of illness. She began her professional dubbing career in 1348. Her roles included Aunt Hetty in Village Stories, Aunt Khanum in Hanna, a Girl on the Farm, and the mother in Honeybee Hutch.

Al Arabiya reported, citing informed sources, that Kata'ib Hezbollah, a group supported by the Islamic Republic, is set to withdraw from the Jurf al-Sakhar area in Iraq within one month based on an agreement that foresees the gradual exit of this group and the deployment of Iraqi security forces. The withdrawal will be phased and simultaneous with the deployment of security forces. This agreement is part of a plan approved by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi concerning the monopoly of weapons by the government.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic of Iran's government, said that people married with 500 toman coins and took ordinary rings for the wedding because they did not have money for an "extravagant" ring. He added that if young people get married, they will be given up to two and a half million toman.

Amir Giti said that Democrats gaining the majority in the US Congress could challenge Donald Trump's administration in budget approval, but would not necessarily prevent military action by the US president against the Islamic Republic. He added that the Trump administration considers naval blockade and economic sanctions effective tools to increase pressure on the Islamic Republic. Giti also said that a change in the composition of Congress does not mean an end to Washington's economic pressures on Tehran.

Jamshid Barzegar said the threat to Persian-speaking media and journalists abroad continues the Islamic Republic's policy to suppress independent reporting. He referred to the trial of two Iranian citizens in the UK accused of spying on Iran International journalists and said Islamic Republic officials deny involvement but openly threaten media with security and military threats. Barzegar added that despite decades of pressure, arrests, and killings of journalists, the Islamic Republic has failed to stop independent reporting and the policy of threats and censorship has become ineffective.

Alireza Kiani said in the program 20 "Fereydoun" that contrary to the common perception, Vahid Khorasani was not seeking the independence of the seminary or a non-governmental religious authority. He was one of seven religious authorities who in 1373 were introduced by the regime as a "permissible religious authority."

The protest group "Cancer Cooler" released a video showing two protesters at a cancer conference in Brussels on Thursday, 28 Aban, going on stage and throwing ashes on Oliver Varhelyi, the EU Commissioner for Health and Animal Welfare. The protesters said this was in opposition to the approval of the "Omnibus X" legal package, which they claim increases the number of toxic pesticides in the food chain. Ursula von der Leyen condemned the behavior and called for an end to physical attacks.

Alireza Kiani referred to Vahid Khorasani's protest and concern for the Shia in Bahrain and Pakistan in the program 20 "Fereydoun," while he has never protested the killing and harassment of Iranians by the Islamic regime.

Houshang Hasan-Yari said the Houthis' attack on the Saudi Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh carries political and economic messages and could reduce foreign investors' confidence. He added that the Houthis use drones and cruise and ballistic missiles to saturate Saudi Arabia's air defense systems. Hasan-Yari said the Houthis have preserved their missile capabilities by modeling after the IRGC and creating underground facilities.

Lord Walney, a member of the British House of Lords, said at an event at Westminster Palace that the struggle of the Iranian people against repression has not been overlooked by British politicians. He emphasized that a free Iran would benefit Britain and the democratic world. He told the Iranian people that a free Iran is something they deserve and its realization benefits the free world.

The office of Prince Reza Pahlavi on X warned that Milad Armoon and Navid Najaran, two political prisoners in the Ekbatan case, face imminent execution after their death sentences were confirmed by the Supreme Court of the Islamic Republic. The office called for action to prevent the executions. The Ekbatan children case relates to the killing of Arman Aliverdi during the November 2022 protests, and in June 2026 it was reported that death sentences were issued for Milad Armoon, Navid Najaran, and two others.

The International Energy Agency said on Thursday that global energy markets may never return to their pre-Iran war structure. The agency stated that countries' actions to secure energy in response to the Iran war could reduce global oil demand by more than four percent by 2035.

The Athletic reported that despite Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement from the Portugal national team and his severe disagreement with Jorge Jesus, sources close to both parties hope that after tensions subside, an official farewell match with Ronaldo's presence will be held to honor his national career. Ronaldo and Jesus did not speak to each other between the October and November international matches. Ronaldo informed the president of the Portuguese Football Federation of his decision to end his national team career one day before the announcement of the player list.

According to Vahid Online, Sadaf Haqbin, a 23-year-old woman from Khomam in Gilan province, was shot dead by her former partner during a party on Tuesday, 27 Aban. The young man entered the party with a hunting rifle, locked the attendees in a room, and after assaulting her and asking for marriage consent, shot her when she refused. Police arrested the suspect who confessed to the murder.

Omid Memarian, a political analyst, said the transfer of US military equipment from Patriot systems to refueling aircraft to Israel indicates increased readiness for a possible attack scenario on the Islamic Republic. He added that with the closure of the diplomatic channel, the likelihood of war has increased compared to last week, but there is a disagreement between the goals of the US and Israel; Trump seeks a nuclear deal and exit from war, while Netanyahu pressures for another attack.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said in an interview with Israel's Channel 12 that he has not yet decided on military action against Iran and is not in a hurry to make this decision. The White House has asked intelligence agencies to assess the consequences of various military plans.

Ghassan Ashour, a Middle East analyst, said that handing over control of Jurf al-Sakhar to Iraqi security forces weakens the political, security, and economic power of Kata'ib Hezbollah. According to him, this area was the only region in Iraq that the group had full control over and used it for economic activities and oil transfer.

Shahir Shahid Thalath said the transfer of US Patriot systems and refueling aircraft to Israel is more precautionary and defensive than preparation for an attack on the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that the US is trying to keep its military equipment out of reach of the Islamic Republic due to the possibility of escalating conflict.
The European Union stated at the IAEA Board of Governors meeting that the agency cannot confirm that the declared nuclear materials of the Islamic Republic have not been diverted from peaceful uses.

Esmail Kowsari, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said that unity and cohesion must be maintained so that the US leaves West Asia and the region establishes its independence and integrity. He added that the enemy tries to open the Strait of Hormuz and attack Iran's nuclear program, but Iran has managed the country for over forty years despite sanctions and blockades.

Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said he considers the possibility of war high but that Arab countries in the region are deeply worried about suffering damage and the spread of war. He stated that if war occurs, US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and the UAE will also be targeted because these countries host US bases. Bakhshayesh Ardestani added that Iranian society is somewhat prepared for building nuclear weapons.

Behrouz Mohibinejadmabadi, the representative of Sabzevar in the parliament, said that the air defense capability of the Islamic Republic has increased in recent months and "F-35 fighter jets will no longer have a safe space in Iranian skies." He added that the Islamic Republic does not accept the condition of "neither war nor peace" and may take actions to break the blockade. He also warned that the Islamic Republic targets "offending" ships and tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and will target any area from which it is attacked.

Ali Belali, advisor to the commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, said the armed forces of the Islamic Republic are fully prepared and ready to respond to any enemy miscalculation, and if any hostile action occurs, the enemy will face missile strikes. He added there are no limitations on the number of missiles or capabilities, and enemies have faced many difficulties countering Iran's missiles. Belali also said that if ordered, there is no limitation on using missile capabilities in new geographic areas.

Hossein Alizadeh, an international affairs analyst, said Trump is postponing the timing of the attack to next year to assess whether economic and attritional pressure against the Islamic Republic will be effective or if military action will be necessary.

A video sent to Iran International shows a citizen beside a road in northern Iran writing the slogans "From Savadkuh to Abdanan, my life is for Iran" and "Forever and a day, long live the Shah" on a wall.

In a volatile game, San Antonio Spurs defeated Los Angeles Clippers 124-112 with Victor Wembanyama's brilliance and returned to the top of the Western Conference with 13 wins and 3 losses. Portland Trail Blazers defeated Milwaukee Bucks 124-114 with a three-point storm by Tommie Kamara and recorded their tenth win of the season.

The Israeli ambassador to the United States stated that if Donald Trump decides to resume military attacks against the Islamic Republic, Israel will once again join the operations alongside the US. He said that planning for joint operations has been underway for months at the highest levels and considered the possible acquisition of chemical and biological weapons by the Islamic Republic a vital threat.

The cultural and artistic complex "Jaryan" in Qom was sealed by judicial order. Leili Golestan announced that the venue for the Jaryan book club event in Qom was sealed. The event was scheduled for Thursday, 28 Aban.

Farzin Karbasi, a journalist and political analyst, said there is a dispute between Kata'ib Hezbollah and the Iraqi government over control of the Jurf al-Sakhar area, and this agreement is fragile. He emphasized that armed groups supported by the Islamic Republic enjoy political, financial, and social support, and the Iraqi government faces serious obstacles in disarming them. According to Karbasi, there is a large gap between the Iraqi government's rhetoric about monopoly on weapons and its practical implementation.

Sky News reported, quoting Rob Magowan, commander of cyber and specialist operations of the British Army, that the UK is conducting offensive cyber operations against the Islamic Republic, Russia, China, and North Korea. Magowan described cyber threats against the UK as "significant" and said these countries must know that cyber operations against the UK will have a cost. He also said the UK is not at war but is in a cyber gray zone and that the UK's National Cyber Force has the capability to infiltrate enemy networks.
A video sent to Iran International shows a protester in Bandar Abbas burning the flag of the Islamic Republic and another citizen chanting "Long live the Shah."
A porter was killed following gunfire by military forces in the border areas of Baneh. This incident occurred today, Friday, 29 Aban.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, said on Friday, 29 Aban, that the Islamic Republic will make every effort for oil exports and negotiations amid reports of loading Iranian oil for export. He also said, "The blockade must be broken."

On Wednesday, 27 Aban, an oil tanker near the coast of Khasab, Oman was targeted by an unknown projectile, causing smoke to rise from the sea surface. The UK Maritime Trade Operations stated the tanker was targeted while exiting the Strait of Hormuz, six nautical miles north of Khasab. All crew members are safe, but the extent of damage and potential environmental pollution are still unknown.

According to information received by Iran International, Abuzar Bargahi, a royalist civil activist and one of the detainees of the December protests, was arrested to serve a five-year prison sentence and transferred to Adelabad Prison in Shiraz. A knowledgeable source said Bargahi was arrested on 7 Aban while giving flowers to citizens in front of his flower shop. This civil activist was initially sentenced to 9 years in prison, but the sentence was reduced to five years in the appeals court.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Islamic Republic has directed attacks on ships towards targeting specific and predictable routes in the Strait of Hormuz. He considered the increase in attacks on regional countries and threats to energy infrastructure in Europe and the US as signs of a more aggressive strategy by the Islamic Republic. Aghaei said the possibility of military conflict still exists and its timing and scale depend on Donald Trump's decision.

Citizens have reacted in messages to Iran International to statements by Masoud Pezeshkian, the president, about saving money and sleeping with a jacket. They have compared Pezeshkian's advice with the current economic situation and the high costs of clothing and marriage expenses.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of the Iran International editorial team, said that a regional will has formed to end the activities of proxy groups of the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that the security and stability of Iraq and other countries in the region are tied to ending the influence of forces affiliated with the Islamic Republic and the monopoly of weapons in the hands of governments.

More than 90% of the workforce in Iran work under short-term temporary contracts or so-called "white signature" contracts; this situation has severely weakened workers' job security. Majid Rahmati stated that in the current law, labor unions and syndicates are not foreseen, and this issue, along with the expansion of temporary contracts, has limited workers' job security and the possibility of collective pursuit of labor rights.

Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Manchester United's new coach made news with drone footage of the practice. The drone operator stated that the flight was fully legal with all necessary permits and insurance. The footage shows training before Manchester United's match against Liverpool, but the main lineup is not confirmed.

A video sent to Iran International shows a fruit vendor protesting the tax set for his business. He points to the costs of house rent and car insurance and says, "How much profit does our load have that the government sets taxes of tens of millions of tomans for it?"

The Public Investment Fund Tower in Riyadh was hit by a missile attributed to the Houthis on Thursday, 28 Aban. The attack caused windows on seven to eight floors to break and damaged parts of the building's metal facade. The Saudi-led coalition said it neutralized the missile threat and initial assessments indicate debris fell and caused damage to the building.

The IAEA Board of Governors meeting focused on verifying the Islamic Republic's safeguards commitments and Tehran's adherence to UN Security Council resolutions ends today. Rafael Grossi, the agency's director general, reported that inspectors have access to Iran's nuclear facilities except for the Bushehr power plant.

Ahmad Vahidi, commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, said at the 'Pioneers of Liberation Congress' that revenge and retribution are our rights and the world will no longer be safe for murderers. He added that part of a great battle has been passed and part remains ahead. Vahidi also said the enemy ships do not dare to come within 500-600 kilometers due to the power of the naval and aerospace forces.

The Secretary-General of Kata'ib Hezbollah called on the members of the group to resume their normal activities and announced that disputes with the Iraqi Prime Minister will be resolved through special channels. According to the agreement, the group's forces will withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar within one month.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial board, said the Islamic Republic is under increasing pressure to break the economic siege as its oil revenue resources near depletion. He suggested the government might try to engage in confrontation earlier to prevent worsening economic crisis and internal protests; however, he considers the start of a full-scale war dependent on decisions by the US and Israel.

A citizen criticized the increase in the price of the drug "Warfarin" in a video sent to Iran International. He said the price of each package of this drug rose from 100,000 tomans in early 1404 to 285,000 tomans in late the same year and is now sold for more than half a million tomans.

Mohammad Javad Haj Ali Akbari, the temporary Friday prayer leader of Tehran, announced that the armed forces have an order for unlimited and borderless action at a designated time. He said that if hostile actions are repeated, the armed forces will be ready to confront any scenario. He also added that the presence of US warships and military forces in the region is a sign of their pressure and erosion.

Bloomberg reported, quoting a senior Israeli Air Force official, that extensive missile attacks by the Islamic Republic during the war revealed weaknesses in Israel's air defense systems but also provided extensive information used to upgrade these systems. The official said the Israeli army was able to upgrade its defense systems within a few days. The 'David's Sling' system was also improved to counter a wider range of ballistic threats and now can handle continuous attacks lasting several weeks.

Leaders of Britain, Germany, and France emphasized European coordination in potential negotiations with Russia and the unrealistic nature of Moscow's conditions at the Berlin meeting. Meanwhile, the US special envoy announced Washington's efforts to reach an agreement with European support and said Russia has not opposed providing security guarantees similar to NATO's Article 5 to Ukraine.

Kazem Nourmofidi, the representative of the Supreme Leader in Golestan province, asked people to help manage energy consumption and ensure stable gas supply by reducing heating device temperatures by three degrees. He said if Tehran, Alborz, and Semnan provinces save gas consumption, better gas supply for northern provinces will be possible. Nourmofidi added that in the short remaining time, full compensation of this reduction through increased production is not possible and consumption management must be used.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, described the statements of the UK's senior military commander about offensive cyber operations against the Islamic Republic as indicating a shift in London's approach from reacting to threats to preventive and retaliatory actions. According to him, the Islamic Republic, Russia, China, and North Korea are attempting to weaken the security and deterrence of the UK and Europe using cyber attacks and hybrid warfare tools, and London is preparing to increase the cost of these actions.

The Instagram page Stadium 19 released a video showing the latest status of Azadi Stadium, indicating that the hybrid grass planting phase has been completed but the stadium tunnels are still under renovation. It was previously planned for the stadium to be ready for the 1406–1405 season, but the complete removal of the previous grass and planting of new grass has prolonged the preparation process.

In the ongoing review of the Iranian National Revolution in Dey 1404, information indicates that the head of the judiciary in Qom province was active in suppressing and confiscating the property of protesters. Farzad Fattahi discusses the protests and suppression in Qom province in the program "Geography of the National Revolution."

Dozens of trucks have stopped in a long queue at the Ramshar fuel station in Zabol county to receive diesel, and drivers say they have waited up to three days for refueling. Station officials have stated that the delay is due to a shortage of diesel. This situation has caused dissatisfaction among drivers and disruption in their work activities.

Yahya Saree, spokesperson for the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic, threatened on Friday, 29 Aban, in response to a warning from the Saudi-led coalition to evacuate the port of Al Hudaydah in western Yemen, that if this port is bombed, Saudi ports on the Red Sea coast will be targeted. Saree said that if the enemy carries out its threats to bomb Al Hudaydah port, the port of Jeddah and all Saudi ports along the Red Sea coast will be targeted by their forces.

Ahmad Alamolhoda, the representative of the Supreme Leader in Khorasan Razavi, said that people have two main concerns: the spread of unveiled women and livelihood issues. He added that people believe their innocent daughters are at risk and are also worried about the livelihood situation.

The public and revolutionary prosecutor of Oshnavieh announced the arrest of six suspects in the case of sexual assault on a woman with a disability in this county. Indictments have been issued for these individuals and their case has been sent to court for trial.

Amin Hayyan, the office manager of Yahya Saree, the spokesperson for the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic, announced that the Al-Shuqaiq power plant in Saudi Arabia will be targeted by the Houthis "within the next few hours." According to Saree, this attack will be "in response to the coalition led by Saudi Arabia's attacks on the Saada and Al-Mokha power plants in Yemen."

Two British men appeared today at the Old Bailey court in London in connection with the Fairford airbase incident. Prosecutors have accused one of them of cooperating with the intelligence service of a foreign country and the other of unauthorized entry into a restricted area with the intent to act against the security of Britain. Police consider this incident an operation in line with the interests of the Islamic Republic's intelligence service.

The National newspaper reported, citing Iraqi, Lebanese, and US security officials, that Islamic Republic agents have been traveling in the Middle East for over two decades using fake or others' passports and IDs, aiding Tehran's allied armed groups. The newspaper wrote that the Revolutionary Guards have expanded their influence over Hezbollah's decision-making in Lebanon during the past three years. Islamic Republic agents also remain present in various parts of Lebanon, especially the south, to support Hezbollah.

Mohammad Ali Abtahi, a reformist political activist, said that the Mossad intelligence agency is behind the hardline currents and efforts to remove Masoud Pezeshkian. Abtahi added that this organization, which can identify the sleeping locations of commanders, can also fuel a hardline atmosphere in Iran's political space.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing items purchased with a two million toman credit from the July ration card for two people and criticized the reduction in purchasing power and government policies. He said the Islamic Republic intends to remove or reduce this amount for some income groups.
